suggestions.reason: The clause clearly defines what the Consultant is engaged to perform and establishes a process for adding work, but it never expressly states that services not described in Exhibit A — and not subsequently authorized by a signed supplemental agreement — are outside the scope of the Contract Services. This omission creates interpretive risk for both parties: the City may argue that related or incidental work is implicitly included, while the Consultant may face disputes over unauthorized out-of-scope work and unpaid compensation. Without an explicit exclusion statement, neither party has a clear contractual baseline against which to measure scope creep or resist informal task expansion.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Any services not described in Exhibit A are expressly outside the scope of the Contract Services unless authorized by a written supplemental agreement or amendment signed by the Parties. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: The compensation clause defers almost entirely to Exhibit A without establishing any of the core commercial mechanics—fee structure, invoice issuance and timing, payment due date, expense treatment, or invoice dispute rights—leaving both the City and the Consultant without enforceable commercial terms in the body of the Agreement itself. The absence of a payment due date creates collection uncertainty for the Consultant, while the lack of an invoice dispute mechanism leaves the City with no defined process to challenge erroneous charges. Neither party has contractual clarity on whether fees are fixed or subject to change, nor on whether expenses are included in or additional to stated compensation. Exhibit A should be revised concurrently to ensure the fee schedule is specified with sufficient detail to be incorporated by reference.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant the fees specified therein for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement, within thirty (30) days following receipt of a valid invoice; provided that the City may dispute any invoice by written notice (email sufficing) within ten (10) Business Days of receipt, and undisputed amounts shall remain due and payable. Fees are fixed as set forth in Exhibit A and may only be modified by written amendment executed by both parties. Expenses shall be reimbursable solely to the extent expressly set forth in Exhibit A.

suggestions.reason: The termination clause omits a cure period for cause-based termination, meaning either party may terminate immediately upon alleging a breach without affording the other an opportunity to remedy it — a material gap from market-standard practice that exposes both the City and Consultant to premature termination without recourse. Additionally, the undefined term "cause" leaves the grounds for non-convenience termination commercially ambiguous, as it does not specify material breach or insolvency as the operative standard, potentially inviting disputes over whether a termination was justified. The Consultant's corresponding termination right also lacks any stated grounds, creating an asymmetry in transparency between the two parties' rights. Note: The existing survival provision covering indemnity and insurance should be confirmed as expressly enumerated in any broader survival clause elsewhere in the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days' prior written notice for convenience, or upon written notice to Consultant for material breach, provided that the breaching party shall have thirty (30) days following such written notice to cure the breach prior to termination becoming effective. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the Agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice for convenience, or upon written notice for material breach, subject to the same thirty (30) day cure period. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted imposes compliance obligations solely on the Consultant and omits several market-standard elements that expose both parties to legal and operational risk: it contains no reference to anti-bribery, anti-corruption, or forced labor and human trafficking prohibitions, leaving both parties without a contractual basis to manage those regulatory exposures. It also fails to allocate the costs of compliance with a change in law — a gap that could generate a mid-performance dispute about which party absorbs new regulatory burdens — and includes no mutual obligation to notify the other party of a known material violation, which limits each party's ability to mitigate harm in a timely manner. Finally, the indemnity in the second sentence should be anchored to the Consultant's own violation, not read as an absolute strict-liability undertaking.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with all applicable local, state, federal, and international rules, regulations, and laws, including those addressing anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and forced labor and human trafficking prohibitions, pertaining to this Agreement, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to herein. Each party shall bear its own costs of compliance with any change in applicable law and shall promptly notify the other party in writing of any known material violation thereof affecting performance under this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on Consultant's violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause addresses anti-discrimination obligations in isolation but omits several market-standard compliance elements, leaving material gaps for both parties: it does not require compliance with anti-bribery and anti-corruption Laws, does not impose any obligation to notify the other party of a breach of Law materially affecting performance, and contains no supply-chain due-diligence standard addressing forced labor, child labor, or human trafficking. As drafted, neither party has a contractual mechanism to identify or respond to compliance failures beyond the narrow anti-discrimination context, creating enforcement gaps and potential regulatory exposure for both the City and Consultant. The reference to specific Kansas statutes should be preserved as minimum floors while the broader compliance obligation is anchored to "all applicable Laws."
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant shall comply with all applicable Laws, including without limitation the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.), the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.), and applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and anti-forced-labor and anti-human-trafficking Laws, and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any breach of applicable Law that materially affects performance of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The insurance maintenance obligation is currently limited to "the duration of this Agreement," leaving a gap for latent claims — particularly under professional liability — that may arise after expiration or termination but relate to work performed during the term; a standard post-term tail period is absent. Additionally, the clause contains no statement clarifying that the procurement and maintenance of insurance does not limit or satisfy either party's liability under the Agreement, creating ambiguity as to whether a policy's coverage limits could be construed as a ceiling on a party's contractual or tortious exposure. Both gaps are commercially material in a professional services context where project-related claims routinely surface after the engagement ends. Note: Ensure any post-term insurance obligation is aligned with the Agreement's survival clause.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years following its expiration or termination, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The procurement and maintenance of such insurance shall not be construed to limit or satisfy either party's liability or obligations under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: The indemnification clause contains three gaps that expose both parties to commercial and enforceability risk. First, the clause is silent on whether it is subject to, or carved out from, any limitation of liability provision elsewhere in the Agreement, creating ambiguity about its interaction with any liability cap and potential for conflicting provisions to override each other unpredictably. Second, the claim-handling mechanics are incomplete: while the Consultant's notice obligation is stated, there is no provision allocating control of the defense or imposing a cooperation obligation on the City, which are market-standard procedural protections that benefit both parties. Third, the absence of any duty on the indemnified party to mitigate its losses is a material omission that could expose the Consultant to unchecked damages that the City took no steps to limit. Note: Ensure this Section is expressly enumerated in any Survival clause to remain operative following expiration or termination of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Subject to any limitation of liability expressly set forth in this Agreement, and without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. Consultant shall give the City prompt written notice (email sufficing) of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision within ten (10) Business Days of Consultant becoming aware thereof; Consultant shall have the right to control the defense of any such claim, the City shall reasonably cooperate in such defense, and the City shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its losses in connection therewith.

suggestions.reason: This disputes clause contains several material deficiencies that expose both the City and the Consultant to significant legal and commercial risk. The clause omits governing law entirely, fails to designate a specific forum for formal proceedings, and uses the permissive "should" rather than "shall" for the negotiation step — meaning neither party is actually obligated to negotiate before filing suit. Most critically, the phrase permitting the initiating party to "take such steps as it deems necessary" confers entirely unbounded, unilateral discretion with no defined forum or time constraint, leaving neither party with predictable or enforceable dispute resolution rights. Finally, the obligation to continue performing during a dispute rests solely on the Consultant, creating an asymmetric burden that is not commercially standard in a bilateral professional services relationship.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 11. Disputes. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of [State]. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement shall first be addressed by good-faith negotiations between the parties for a period of thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute within such period, either party may pursue its claims exclusively in the state or federal courts located in [County, State]; provided, however, that either party may seek emergency injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction without first exhausting the negotiation period. Notwithstanding any such dispute, both parties shall continue to perform their respective obligations under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: The existing representations clause is limited solely to an anti-collusion statement, leaving the agreement without any warranty of service quality, legal compliance, or non-infringement — the three core protections that market-standard professional services agreements require for both parties' benefit. Without a performance standard, neither party has an agreed benchmark against which the Services can be measured or disputed; without a law compliance warranty, both parties bear unallocated regulatory risk; and without a non-infringement warranty and an express breach remedy, neither party has a clear path to relief if the deliverables expose the other to third-party claims. The absence of these elements renders the Representations clause commercially deficient and legally inadequate as a bilateral risk allocation mechanism. Note: Confirm that any warranty obligations added here are expressly enumerated in the Agreement's survival clause to remain enforceable post-termination.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Each party warrants that it will comply with all applicable laws in connection with this Agreement. Provider further warrants that the Services will be performed with reasonable skill and care and that the Services and deliverables will not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights; in the event of a breach of the foregoing warranty, Provider shall, at its election, re-perform the non-conforming Services or refund the fees paid for such Services.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is unilateral, requiring only the Consultant to warrant that it has the requisite power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement; no corresponding representation is made by the Client. This asymmetry creates an enforceability gap: if the Client lacks proper corporate authorization, the Agreement could be challenged as unenforceable, yet the Consultant bears the full burden of that risk without any corresponding assurance from the other side. Market-standard professional services agreements require both parties to make mutual authority representations to establish a sound contractual foundation for each party's benefit.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement, and the individuals who have signed this Agreement on behalf of each party have the legal power, right, and authority to do so and to bind such party.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters" is undefined, subjective, and would likely require extrinsic evidence to interpret, creating an objectively unenforceable standard that neither party can reliably rely upon or plan against. The warranty that all work "shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards" contains no materiality qualifier, exposing Consultant to unlimited liability for any deviation, however minor, while providing Customer with a correspondingly unlimited claim right that is commercially disproportionate and difficult to bound. Additionally, the final sentence imposes a unilateral capability warranty solely on Consultant with no corresponding obligation on Customer to provide the information and cooperation reasonably necessary for Consultant to meet that standard, creating a structurally imbalanced provision. Replacing the vague "state of the art" formulation with an objective "industry-standard" benchmark, inserting a materiality threshold, and adding a reciprocal information-and-cooperation duty on Customer restores bilateral commercial balance.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform in all material respects to the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of industry-standard procedures and techniques applicable to the relevant subject matter. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services, provided that Customer shall furnish Consultant with all reasonably necessary information and cooperation to enable such performance.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the assignment restriction binds only the Consultant while imposing no equivalent limitation on the City, creating an asymmetric clause that is commercially one-sided. The consent right is unqualified — there is no "not unreasonably withheld" standard, no response deadline, and no carve-out for affiliate transfers or business succession events such as a merger or acquisition, which could expose either party to an inadvertent breach in routine corporate transactions. Additionally, the clause is silent on continuing liability of the assigning party after transfer, on notice obligations, and on either party's rights upon a change of control, all of which are market-standard elements in professional services agreements. Left unaddressed, these gaps could result in disputed assignments, termination uncertainty, or unenforced obligations following a corporate restructuring by either party.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and to be provided within fifteen (15) days of written request; provided, however, that either party may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor entity in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all of its assets, upon written notice to the other party, with the assigning party remaining liable for its obligations hereunder unless expressly released in writing by the other party. In the event of a change of control of either party, the other party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. This Agreement is binding upon the permitted successors and assigns of both parties.

suggestions.reason: The notice block identifies Columbia Capital Management, LLC's current address and designated recipient but contains no mechanism by which either party may update its notice details over the life of the Agreement. Without such a provision, a party that relocates, changes its designated contact, or updates its address has no contractually recognized method to do so, creating a risk that notices sent to a stale address are nonetheless deemed valid and effective. This gap could result in a party legitimately missing time-sensitive communications — such as notices of breach, termination, or indemnity claims — through no fault of its own, to the prejudice of either side equally.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice details by providing at least ten (10) days' prior written notice to the other party in accordance with this Section.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, this clause omits three market-standard elements that together create meaningful legal and commercial exposure for both parties. First, the absence of any statement that neither party may bind the other leaves open an apparent-authority risk that could expose either the City or Consultant to obligations neither intended to assume. Second, the tax-responsibility language is unilateral — it addresses only Consultant's taxes and withholdings while leaving the City's obligations regarding its own personnel's costs and benefits unstated, creating an asymmetric and incomplete allocation. Third, without an express statement that Consultant controls the manner and means of performing the Services, the clause lacks the foundational control-test language that courts and tax authorities rely upon to confirm independent-contractor status, increasing misclassification risk for both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who shall control the manner and means by which it performs the Services. Each party shall be responsible for all compensation, taxes, and withholdings applicable to its own employees and personnel, and Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability with respect to any taxes or withholdings owed on compensation paid to Consultant under this Agreement. Neither party shall have authority to bind or obligate the other party. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: This section addresses only the Kansas Cash-Basis Law budgetary appropriation framework, leaving the Agreement silent on several market-standard compliance obligations that create bilateral legal exposure. Without anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and supply-chain labor standards provisions, neither party has a contractual baseline for conduct that could expose the other to regulatory liability. The absence of a mutual duty to notify upon a material breach of applicable law, and the failure to allocate the cost burden of any change in law, also create operational ambiguity that could become contentious mid-performance. Note: To the extent any surviving compliance obligations are added, they should be expressly enumerated in the Agreement's Survival clause.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein. Each party shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including those governing anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and the prohibition of forced labor and child labor in its supply chain; shall promptly notify the other party in writing (email sufficing) upon discovering any breach of applicable law that materially affects this Agreement; and shall each bear its own costs of compliance with any change in applicable law during the term of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The current clause identifies governing law but is structurally incomplete as a dispute resolution provision: it names no forum, imposes no pre-dispute escalation requirement, creates no mutual or symmetric forum obligation binding both parties equally, contains no carve-out preserving urgent injunctive relief, and is silent on whether obligations continue while a dispute is pending. For a Professional Services Agreement, this leaves both parties exposed to parallel litigation in unintended jurisdictions, with no mechanism to contain costs before formal proceedings commence and no certainty that performance will continue during a dispute. These are market-standard elements that courts and commercial practitioners expect to see in any governing law or dispute resolution section of a professional services contract.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 19. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas. Prior to initiating formal proceedings, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith negotiation for thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. Any unresolved dispute shall be submitted exclusively to the state or federal courts located in Kansas, to whose jurisdiction both parties irrevocably submit. Either party may seek urgent injunctive or equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without first completing such negotiation, and each party shall continue performing its obligations under this Agreement pending resolution of any dispute.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is ambiguous as to mechanism and standard: one reasonable reading treats the reformation as self-executing between the parties with no judicial involvement, while another requires a court to actively rewrite the provision, and neither reading is commanded by the text. This ambiguity leaves both parties uncertain whether a defective provision is effectively cured without further action or whether its status remains contested until a court rules, which could disrupt the enforceability of related provisions in the interim. Replacing "automatically reformed" with the market-standard objective benchmark — modification to the minimum extent necessary to achieve validity — gives a court a judicially administrable directive and eliminates the interpretive dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable under applicable law, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by such modification, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the waiver clause does not expressly state that a party's waiver of one specific breach or right is limited to that instance and does not operate as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right. This gap creates a material enforceability risk for both parties: a court could interpret an isolated, written waiver granted by one party as evidence of a broader, ongoing relinquishment of related rights, undermining the protections that the clause otherwise intends to preserve. Market-standard waiver provisions include an explicit "single instance" limitation to close this interpretive gap and protect both parties equally from inadvertent over-waiver arguments.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party. Any such written waiver shall be limited solely to the specific breach or instance for which it is granted and shall not operate as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach, default, or right under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The current clause omits three market-standard elements: it does not require signatures by an authorized representative of each party (leaving open the risk that any employee's signature could purportedly bind a party), it does not expressly extend the amendment requirement to schedules and exhibits (which frequently contain material commercial terms), and it contains no anti-oral-modification or anti-course-of-conduct language (meaning either party could argue that subsequent conduct or verbal exchanges altered the Agreement). Collectively, these gaps create meaningful enforceability uncertainty for both parties, particularly in disputes over the effect of email exchanges, side letters, or operational accommodations made during performance.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including all schedules and exhibits hereto, may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by an authorized representative of each party; no oral agreement or course of conduct shall constitute or be deemed an amendment hereof.

suggestions.reason: The survivorship clause names only Consultant's post-termination obligations—Insurance and Indemnification—while imposing no corresponding surviving obligations on Client, creating a bilateral imbalance that leaves Client's reciprocal duties (most notably payment of accrued fees) potentially extinguished at termination. Additionally, the residual catch-all—"any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination"—is too indeterminate to be reliably enforced, as two reasonable counsel would disagree on which provisions it captures, exposing either party to dispute over operative post-termination rights. Replacing the subjective phrase with "by their express terms or nature are intended to survive termination" provides an objective, judicially recognized standard. Note: Any provisions added to the survival enumeration here should also be cross-checked against any general survival clause elsewhere in the Agreement to ensure consistency.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), Client's obligation to pay any accrued and unpaid fees, each party's confidentiality obligations, and any other provisions that by their express terms or nature are intended to survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The compliance covenant in the final sentence is imposed exclusively on Consultant — requiring it to "act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" — without imposing any corresponding obligation on the City, creating an asymmetry that is not commercially justified given that both parties have performance obligations under the Agreement. As drafted, the City assumes no express duty to comply with the Agreement's terms or applicable law, which undermines bilateral enforceability. Additionally, the phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is objectively ambiguous — it is undefined, unanchored to any jurisdiction or regulatory framework, and two reasonable lawyers would reach different conclusions as to its scope, exposing the clause to interpretive disputes. Both deficiencies are remedied by converting the covenant to a mutual obligation and replacing the vague law reference with a standard formulation.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, each Party agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable federal, state, and local Laws governing this undertaking.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes an unlimited, open-ended fiduciary standard on the Consultant — including the full prudent-person duty of care — without any cross-reference to, or carve-out preserving, the Agreement's limitation of liability provisions, thereby exposing the Consultant to potentially uncapped financial liability for any failure in asset management judgment. At the same time, the clause is entirely one-sided: it places all operative obligations on the Consultant while imposing no corresponding duty on the Client to provide accurate information or reasonable cooperation, which could impair the Consultant's ability to discharge the very fiduciary standard demanded. The "enterprise of like character and with like aims" benchmark, while drawn from ERISA case law, remains sufficiently abstract that two courts could reach different conclusions on the applicable standard of care in a dispute, creating enforceability uncertainty. Note: The limitation of liability provision elsewhere in the Agreement should be reviewed to confirm it expressly governs fiduciary duty claims, except for gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement, subject to the limitation of liability provisions of this Agreement except in cases of gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims. Client shall provide Consultant with reasonably requested information and cooperation necessary for Consultant to discharge its fiduciary obligations hereunder.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" imposes a delivery obligation on the City without anchoring it to any objective timeframe, meaning both parties would be left to dispute after the fact whether the City's response was sufficiently prompt. This ambiguity creates an enforcement gap: the Consultant cannot rely on a predictable information flow to execute the investment plan, while the City has no clear standard against which its performance can be measured. Replacing the vague standard with a defined number of Business Days following written request gives both parties an objective, court-enforceable benchmark and eliminates the need for extrinsic evidence to determine breach.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts within five (5) Business Days following Consultant's written request therefor.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "properly determine required liquidity" is commercially ambiguous because neither "required liquidity" nor the standard for determining it is defined anywhere in the clause, leaving both parties without an objective benchmark to assess whether the Consultant's analysis meets its obligations or whether the City's data disclosures are sufficient. This ambiguity could give rise to disputes — the City may contend that any liquidity estimate exceeds its mandate, while the Consultant may argue the data provided was inadequate to perform a sound analysis. Anchoring the liquidity determination to the applicable investment plan provides an objective, document-internal reference point that constrains the concept for both parties equally.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to determine the liquidity requirements necessary to implement the applicable investment plan.

suggestions.reason: This clause places a binding custodial instruction obligation on the City that is entirely contingent on confirmations provided by Consultant, yet imposes no corresponding timing obligation on Consultant to deliver those confirmations, nor any timeframe within which the City must act once confirmations are received. This asymmetry is commercially problematic: the City bears settlement risk and potential liability for delayed transactions if Consultant fails to furnish confirmations in a timely manner, while Consultant faces no corresponding duty. Without objective time anchors on both sides, the clause is unenforceable as a practical workflow and exposes either party to disputes over whether instructions were given or confirmations were delivered within a commercially reasonable period.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, within two (2) Business Days following receipt of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant, which Consultant shall deliver within one (1) Business Day following each such transaction.

suggestions.reason: Although the clause identifies certain conflict scenarios and establishes a limited investment policy to manage them, it contains no affirmative obligation on Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to the City as they arise. The absence of a disclosure requirement is a material gap: without it, neither party has a defined mechanism for surfacing conflicts in real time, leaving the City without the information needed to make informed decisions and exposing Consultant to allegations of concealment. This imbalance undermines the enforceability of the conflict-management framework the clause purports to establish and creates reputational and fiduciary risk for both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time. Consultant shall promptly disclose to the City in writing any actual or potential conflict of interest of which Consultant becomes aware that may affect the services provided under this Agreement, and the City shall have the right to direct Consultant on how to proceed upon receipt of such disclosure.

suggestions.reason: This clause contains four compounding deficiencies that create material enforceability risk for both parties. The reference to "Schedule X" is an unfilled placeholder, leaving the scope of authorized representatives legally indeterminate. The City's unilateral right to amend that Schedule "at any time" with no defined notice period provides Consultant with no minimum window to operationally adjust to changed authority structures, which is commercially one-sided and operationally unworkable. Additionally, the Consultant's right to use City Account information in aggregate performance data is entirely unreciprocated — the City is afforded no corresponding consent mechanism or opt-out right, creating an asymmetric grant that a court could read broadly against either party.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule [___] to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon at least ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City, provided that the City may, upon written notice to Consultant, require Consultant to exclude such information from future aggregate performance data.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes the fee rate and billing frequency but omits several commercially essential payment mechanics that expose both parties to dispute: there is no stated payment due date after an invoice is issued, no mechanism for either party to contest an incorrect invoice, no consequence (such as interest) for overdue amounts, and no clarity on whether the fee rate is fixed or subject to revision. Without a payment due date and late-payment remedy, neither party has an objective benchmark to enforce or contest collection; without an invoice dispute procedure, the paying party has no contractual process to challenge a miscalculated quarterly bill. The partial expense carve-out ("sole compensation") also lacks explicit treatment of pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses, leaving ambiguity about whether such costs are borne by Consultant or billed separately.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts (which rate may be amended upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party), billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000, and with payment due within thirty (30) days following receipt of each invoice. Either party may dispute an invoice by written notice within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and undisputed amounts shall remain due and payable as stated; overdue undisputed amounts shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is less. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, excluding any pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses billed separately. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause addresses only Consultant's regulatory registration status and leaves three material gaps that create legal and commercial uncertainty for both parties: (1) no representation that Services will comply with applicable laws beyond the Consultants Act registration, (2) no warranty that the Services will be free of third-party intellectual property infringement, exposing the City to downstream liability, and (3) no stated warranty period or remedy upon breach, leaving both parties without an agreed framework to resolve deficient performance. Without a defined remedy, disputes over whether Consultant must re-perform or refund fees will require litigation to resolve, increasing cost and risk for both sides.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act"); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; and (iv) warrants throughout the term of this Agreement that the Services comply with all applicable laws and do not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights, and upon breach of such warranty shall re-perform the affected Services or refund the fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes the Consultant's fiduciary status but omits any express standard of skill, care, or diligence by which the Consultant's performance is to be measured. Without a stated performance standard, neither party has an objective contractual benchmark for assessing whether the Consultant has discharged its obligations, creating ambiguity that could impair the Client's ability to bring a claim for underperformance and leave the Consultant without clear guidance on the level of conduct expected. Market-standard professional services agreements pair a fiduciary declaration with an express professional skill-and-care standard to give the provision practical enforceability.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant is a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement and shall perform its services with the skill, care, and diligence reasonably expected of a qualified professional in its field;

suggestions.reason: The authority-to-contract representation is stated solely for the Consultant, leaving the other party's capacity entirely unaddressed. From a neutral commercial standpoint, this creates an asymmetric risk: if the other party lacked proper corporate or organizational authorization to execute the Agreement, neither party would have a contractual basis to challenge that deficiency or seek rescission. Market-standard practice in professional services agreements requires both parties to make equivalent capacity and authority representations to ensure mutual enforceability from the outset.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents that it is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
